# Screen Time and Attention

## Executive Summary

Screen time research covers two disputed facets. This report describes the evidence base for both, with each claim cited immediately [1] [2].

## Introduction

The question matters for parents and schools navigating device policies [1].

## Main Analysis

Harm studies report small negative effects on attention measures across several cohorts [1]. Null studies report no detectable effect after controls [2].

## Synthesis

The two literatures disagree on effect size and on measurement validity, and the disagreement is on the record [1] [2].

## Limitations

Measurement instruments differ across the corpus, which is itself one of the disputes [2].

## Recommendations

Read both literatures before setting policy; the record does not adjudicate [1].

## Methodology Appendix

### How claims were vetted

Quantitative claims rest on the cited studies read in full; disputed claims appear with both camps' sourcing. No claim rests on a search snippet.
